items.stem:

items.answer: (i) 24% of 500 = 120. (ii) Through air (droplets). (iii) none of them. (iv) Spread awareness about covering the mouth and nose while sneezing and washing hands.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Cases of diarrhoea rose in a village after a pipeline leaked near a drain. As a health worker, explain the cause and list three actions you would recommend.
items.answer: Sewage entered the drinking water and spread water-borne germs. Actions: boil or chlorinate drinking water; repair the leak; use ORS for patients; wash hands before eating.

items.stem: Which of these diseases does NOT spread through contaminated food and water?

items.stem: What is meant by antibodies?
items.answer: Proteins made by white blood cells that fight specific pathogens
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Antibodies – proteins made by white blood cells that fight specific pathogens.

items.stem: How does a vaccine protect us without making us ill?
items.answer: It contains dead or weakened microbes that cannot cause disease but make the body produce antibodies; these protect when the real microbe enters.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakened/dead microbe. 1 mark: antibodies ready.

items.stem: A child has a viral fever. Her uncle suggests giving her leftover antibiotic tablets. What would you advise, and why?
items.answer: Do not give them: antibiotics do not act on viruses; leftover doses may be wrong and can cause side effects and resistance. Consult a doctor; give rest, fluids.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: advice. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem: Rahul cut his knee while playing. Two days later, the wound was red, swollen and warm. Explain what was happening in his body.
items.answer: Germs entered the wound; white blood cells gathered to fight them, causing redness, swelling and warmth as part of the immune response.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: infection. 1 mark: WBC response.

items.stem: Explain why polio drops are given to all young children in a pulse polio drive on the same day across India.
items.answer: Vaccinating all children together builds immunity in the whole community at once, so the virus cannot find unprotected children to infect and spread.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: all at once. 1 mark: stops spread.

items.stem:
Read: Aditi's baby brother has a vaccination card listing BCG at birth, OPV drops, and MMR at 9 months. Her neighbour says vaccines are unnecessary because the baby looks healthy.
(i) Which disease does BCG protect against? (ii) What does a vaccine contain? (iii) How does it protect? (iv) How would you reply to the neighbour?
items.answer: (i) Tuberculosis. (ii) Dead or weakened microbes. (iii) Makes the body produce antibodies so it is ready when the real microbe attacks. (iv) Vaccines prevent disease before it happens; healthy babies need them to stay protected.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: When almost every child in a city is vaccinated against measles, even the few unvaccinated babies are protected. Explain why.
items.answer: The virus cannot find enough people to infect, so it cannot spread in the community; this indirect protection is called herd immunity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: chain of spread broken. 1 mark: community/herd protection.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The ability of the body to resist and fight disease-causing microbes."
items.answer: immunity
items.markingKey: (d) Immunity is the ability of the body to resist and fight disease-causing microbes.

items.stem: A child is given an antibiotic for a bacterial infection, feels better after two days and stops taking it. A week later the illness returns and the same medicine does not work well. Explain.
items.answer: The surviving bacteria were the more resistant ones; they multiplied, so the infection returned and the antibiotic is now less effective (antibiotic resistance).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: survivors. 1 mark: resistance develops.

items.answer: (i) 50/200 × 100 = 25%. (ii) Obesity, type 2 diabetes, hypertension (any two). (iii) Daily sports period, healthy canteen food, screen-time awareness (any two). (iv) Habits formed now continue into adulthood and raise the risk of heart disease and diabetes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.
